_note: Cue cards are the ones named in the Month 1 plan; the 'You should say' lines are generic scaffolding written for the app. Part 1 and Part 3 questions are fallbacks used only where the course has no better ones.

skill-long.title: Describe a skill that took you a long time to learn.
say: when and how you learned it
and explain how you feel about it now

person-admire.title: Describe a person you admire.
say: and explain why you admire them

object-daily.title: Describe an object you use every day.
say: how long you have had it
and explain why it matters to you

person-career.title: Describe a person who influenced your career.
say: how you met or know them
and explain how they influenced your career

event-busy.title: Describe a time when you were extremely busy.
say: and explain how you felt about it

place-relax.title: Describe a place you go to relax.
say: and explain why it helps you relax

event-celebration.title: Describe a celebration you enjoyed.
say: and explain why you enjoyed it

experience-mistake.title: Describe a time you learned something from a mistake.
say: and explain how it changed what you do

media-app.title: Describe a website or app you use often.
say: and explain why you use it so often

experience-helped.title: Describe a time you helped someone.
say: and explain how you felt afterwards

object-tech.title: Describe a piece of technology you couldn't live without.
say: and explain why you couldn't live without it

place-nature.title: Describe a natural place you would like to visit.
say: and explain why you would like to go

media-news.title: Describe a news story that caught your attention.
say: where you read or heard it
and explain how you felt about it

media-book.title: Describe a book or film that changed your mind about something.
say: when you read or watched it
what it changed your mind about
and explain why it had that effect

place-env.title: Describe an environmental problem in the area where you live.
say: and explain what could be done about it

event-decision.title: Describe a time you had to make a difficult decision.
say: and explain how you feel about it now

event-proud.title: Describe a time you were proud of a family member.
say: and explain why you were proud

event-journey.title: Describe a journey that didn't go as planned.
say: and explain what you learned from it

object-expensive.title: Describe an expensive thing you bought.
say: and explain whether it was worth the money

event-tradition.title: Describe a family tradition.
say: and explain why it is important to your family

object-gift.title: Describe a gift you gave that someone loved.
say: and explain why they loved it

person-teacher.title: Describe a teacher who influenced you.
say: and explain how they influenced you

place-public.title: Describe a public place that needs improving.
say: and explain how it could be improved

experience-wait.title: Describe a time you had to wait for something.
say: and explain how you felt about it

experience-advice.title: Describe a piece of advice you received.
say: and explain why it was useful or not

event-goal.title: Describe a goal you achieved.
say: and explain how you felt when you achieved it

experience-opinion.title: Describe a time you changed your opinion.
say: what made you change your mind
and explain how you feel about it now

person-job.title: Describe a person who is very good at their job.
say: how you know about their work
and explain why you think they are so good at it

event-goal-now.title: Describe a goal you are working towards.
say: what you are doing to achieve it
and explain how you will feel when you reach it

work: What do you enjoy most about it?
Is there anything you'd change about your job?
mornings: What do you do first thing in the morning?
Has your morning routine changed over the years?
weather: What kind of weather do you like most?
Does the weather affect your mood?
What do people in your country do when it is very hot?
home: Do you live in a house or a flat?
Would you like to move somewhere else one day?
hometown: What do you like most about it?
Has it changed much since you were a child?
free time: What do you do in your free time?
Do you prefer to relax alone or with other people?
Is there a hobby you would like to try?
reading: What kind of books do you read?
Do you prefer paper books or e-books?
music: What kind of music do you like?
Has your taste in music changed?
transport: How do you usually get to work?
Is public transport good where you live?
Would you like to travel differently?
shopping: Do you prefer to shop online or in shops?
What was the last thing you bought?
sport: Is sport popular in your country?
Did you do sport as a child?
neighbours: Do you know your neighbours well?
How important is it to have good neighbours?
Have you ever helped a neighbour?
holidays: Do you like going on holiday?
Where did you go on your last holiday?
Do you prefer holidays at home or abroad?
cooking: What is a dish you can make well?
clothes: What kind of clothes do you like?
Do you wear different clothes for work and for relaxing?
the internet: How often do you use the internet?
What do you mostly use it for?
Do you think people spend too much time online?
friends: How often do you see them?
photographs: Do you print your photos or keep them on your phone?
Who takes the most photos in your family?
sleep: How many hours do you usually sleep?
What do you do when you cannot sleep?
weekends: What do you usually do at weekends?
Do you prefer weekdays or weekends?
How would you spend a perfect weekend?

skills: Which skills matter most for young people today?
Is it better to learn a skill from a teacher or online on your own?
Why do some adults stop learning new things?
How might the skills people need change in the next 20 years?
Should schools teach more practical skills and fewer academic subjects?
work: Why do some people change jobs often?
How has the way people work changed in your lifetime?
Is it more important to earn a high salary or to enjoy your work?
Do you think more people will work from home in the future?
What qualities make someone a good manager?
cities: What are the advantages of living in a big city?
Why do many young people move to cities?
How could cities be made better places to live?
Do you think cities will keep growing?
What problems do large cities have?
Is it better to live in a city or the countryside?
technology: How has technology changed the way people communicate?
What would happen if the internet stopped working for a week?
Do you think technology makes people lonelier?
How might technology change education in the next 20 years?
Are older people able to keep up with technology?
environment: What are the biggest environmental problems today?
Who is more responsible for protecting the environment, governments or individuals?
What would happen if people stopped recycling?
Do you think people will care more about the environment in future?
How can schools teach children to protect nature?
Is it fair to ask poorer countries to reduce pollution?
media: How do people get their news today?
Do you think the news is reliable?
What effect does social media have on young people?
Should the media be controlled by the government?
How might the media change in the future?
Why do people enjoy reading about famous people?
decisions: Who should make important decisions in a family?
Why do some people find it hard to make decisions?
Should young people be given more responsibility?
What would happen if leaders made decisions without consulting anyone?
How do people's decisions change as they get older?
Is it better to decide quickly or to take your time?
family: How have families changed over the past few decades?
What can older and younger generations learn from each other?
Is it important for families to eat meals together?
Do you think parents spend enough time with their children?
How might family life change in the future?
Why do some people live with their parents as adults?
travel: Why do so many people like to travel?
What are the effects of tourism on local people?
Do you think travelling teaches you more than studying?
What would happen if tourists stopped visiting a popular place?
How has travel changed in recent years?
Is it better to travel alone or in a group?
shopping: How has online shopping changed the way people buy things?
Do you think people buy too many things they do not need?
What influences what people decide to buy?
Will shops disappear in the future?
Is it a good idea to buy expensive things?
consumerism: Why do people want to own the latest products?
What are the effects of advertising on children?
Do you think people are happier when they own more?
What could be done to reduce waste?
How might the way we buy things change in the future?
Should companies be responsible for what they sell?
education: What is the purpose of education?
How important are teachers compared with technology?
Do you think children should have homework?
What will schools look like in 20 years?
government: What should governments spend more money on?
How much should the government control people's lives?
Why do some people not vote?
Do you think leaders today are better than in the past?
How can the government encourage people to be healthier?
Should the government support the arts?
society: What are the biggest problems facing society today?
Do people help each other as much as they used to?
How can communities be made stronger?
Is the gap between rich and poor growing?
What would happen if there were no rules?
advice: Who do people usually ask for advice?
Is advice from friends better than advice from experts?
Why do some people ignore advice?
Should young people always follow the advice of older people?
How has the internet changed the way people look for advice?
What makes someone a good adviser?
health: What can people do to stay healthy?
Is it the government's job to make people healthier?
Why do some people find it hard to exercise?
How has people's lifestyle changed in your country?
Do you think people eat worse than in the past?
How might healthcare change in the future?
ambition: What does success mean to people in your country?
Is it better to be ambitious or to be content?
How do people balance work and personal life?
Why do some people work too much?
What advice would you give someone starting their career?
How might attitudes to work change in the next generation?
